categories.title: Block poster makers
categories.intro: Turn one image into sheets you can print, trim and assemble.

items.name: PosterSheet
items.description: A free block poster maker for JPG, PNG and WebP images. Choose A4, Letter, A3 or custom paper, set margins and overlap, then export a multi-page PDF with optional assembly guidance.
items.note: Image processing stays in your browser. Up to 100 poster sheets; no signup or watermark.

items.name: The Rasterbator
items.description: Enlarge an image into a multi-page poster PDF, with halftone styles for wall art.
items.note: Its official FAQ also explains how to select a style without the dot effect.

items.name: PosteRazor
items.description: A wizard-based image-to-poster tool that saves a multi-page PDF. The project offers desktop downloads and a WebAssembly browser version.
items.note: Useful when comparing desktop and browser workflows; check platform compatibility before installing.

categories.title: Image preparation
categories.intro: Prepare the pixels before you decide how large to print.

items.name: GIMP
items.description: A desktop editor for cropping, retouching and preparing the artwork before it reaches a block poster maker.
items.note: Keep a copy of the original image so you can revise your crop later.

items.name: GIMP: Print Size
items.description: Explains the relationship between physical print dimensions and image resolution without changing the pixel count.
items.note: Changing the PPI setting alone does not create more image detail.

items.name: GIMP: Scale Image
items.description: Describes resampling and how changing pixel dimensions affects the image and its memory use.
items.note: Use this to distinguish resizing the pixels from changing the intended print size.

items.name: ImageMagick
items.description: Convert, crop and resize images in repeatable workflows before laying them out for printing.
items.note: Best suited to people comfortable with command-line image processing.

categories.title: Paper, printing and assembly
categories.intro: Choose the right stock and avoid accidentally scaling your tiles twice.

items.name: Adobe Acrobat: Print posters and banners
items.description: Explains Poster printing for an oversized PDF, including tile scale, overlap, cut marks and labels.
items.note: For an already tiled PosterSheet PDF, print at Actual Size / 100% instead of tiling it again.

items.name: PosterSheet: Print a large image on multiple pages
items.description: A practical entry point for turning an image into a printable PDF and joining its sheets into a larger poster.
items.note: Match the printer paper to the export setting, and test one sheet first.

items.name: PosterSheet: A4 vs Letter
items.description: Compare A4 and US Letter dimensions and understand why switching paper sizes changes the printable area.
items.note: A4 is 210 × 297 mm; Letter is 215.9 × 279.4 mm.

items.name: PosterSheet: Standard poster sizes
items.description: Explore common poster dimensions in inches and centimeters before choosing your final wall size.
items.note: Margins and repeated overlap affect the sheet count, so check the actual export preview.

categories.title: Artwork and reuse guidance
categories.intro: Find printable artwork and read the rights information attached to each item.

items.name: The Met: Open Access
items.description: Find public-domain artwork images made available through The Metropolitan Museum of Art's Open Access initiative.
items.note: Choose items marked Open Access and download the full-resolution image.

items.name: National Gallery of Art: Free images and Open Access
items.description: A starting point for downloading artwork images available under the National Gallery of Art's Open Access policy.
items.note: Check the individual artwork page and its image availability before planning your poster.

items.name: Wikimedia Commons: Reusing content
items.description: Explains how to reuse Commons images outside Wikimedia, including in print.
items.note: Read each file's license and attribution requirements; the collection does not have one blanket image license.

categories.title: Tools for developers
categories.intro: Building blocks for image previews, PDF output and image processing.

items.name: pdf-lib
items.description: Create and modify PDFs, embed images and draw page content in JavaScript environments, including browsers.
items.note: Useful for generating tiled documents; it is a library, not a ready-made poster layout engine.

items.name: PDF.js
items.description: Mozilla's web standards-based platform for parsing and rendering PDF documents.
items.note: Useful for previewing exported pages; it does not replace a physical print check.

items.name: sharp
items.description: Image processing for Node.js, including resizing, conversion and compositing.
items.note: Appropriate for build scripts and server-side image workflows, rather than direct browser use.

items.name: MDN: Canvas tutorial
items.description: Learn to draw images and graphics with the browser Canvas API, a useful foundation for poster previews.
items.note: Canvas dimensions and memory limits matter when working with large images.
